subject: chickens
one_liner: A dating app for chickens where eight roosters pay to be seen first, then settle it by waking the farmer.
brand_voice_notes: Apply the frozen anti-ai-slop skill throughout. Write as a dating service that considers these outcomes normal. The chickens are the users; their vanity, need for approval and competitive courtship drive the jokes. Explain food stealing and social rank through actions. Keep controls plain, consequences specific and fictional testimonials in the chickens' own voices. Credit the worst AI studio ever discreetly.
demo_screen_concept: One discovery screen shows a large chicken profile card, with Matches and Messages beside it on desktop. The opening profile is Mabel, 18 yards away, photographed beside a breakfast bowl. Her bio reads: 'I take first pick at breakfast.' Pass and Like buttons advance the stack. Liking Mabel produces a mutual-match panel because she has already liked the visitor's rooster profile. Opening the conversation reveals her message: 'Bring dinner. You know which worms I like.' A suggested reply, 'I'll bring two,' can be sent and appears in the thread. A clearly labelled sample boost activates a 30-minute promotion and reveals the yard's activity panel: eight promoted roosters, with messages promising progressively earlier morning calls, ending at 03:40. This demonstrates the competition without claiming that a boost guarantees matches. A profile thumbnail shows the visitor's imposing fence portrait; opening it reveals the uncropped photograph of a small rooster standing on an overturned feed bucket. On mobile, the profile stack occupies the main screen and matches, chat and profile details open in dismissible panels within the same interface.

hero.h1: Your love life woke the farmer.
hero.sub: Strut lets chickens swipe on nearby profiles, match and send messages. Pay to be seen first, then crow before the other seven roosters who bought the same boost. Dawn now starts at 3:40.

observations.behavior: People use flattering profile photographs to imply physical qualities they cannot maintain in person.
observations.mechanic: Select and crop a lead photograph for a swipeable dating profile, hiding the feed bucket that raises a small rooster above the fence.
observations.consequence: The impressive portrait wins a date who steps over the actual rooster. He brings the bucket to their next meeting to preserve the advertised height.

observations.behavior: Someone hungry for approval treats attention from a person who exploits them as evidence that the relationship is improving.
observations.mechanic: A paid likes list reveals a familiar hen; mutual liking opens a private conversation where the rooster proposes dinner.
observations.consequence: The hen who already steals his breakfast gains a willing dinner delivery service. He pays a subscription to discover another meal he can provide.

observations.behavior: People purchase visibility to get ahead of romantic rivals, then escalate their performance when those rivals purchase the same advantage.
observations.mechanic: Timed profile boosts promote several nearby roosters simultaneously. Their match conversations become competing promises of earlier morning calls.
observations.consequence: Paid attention produces a crowing contest at 3:40. The farmer covers the competing roosters' coops while their intended audience sleeps through the result.

editorial_plan.composition_plan: Primary action: Find a match, opening the discovery demo. Recognizable product visual: a large chicken portrait in a swipeable profile stack, Pass and Like controls beneath it, and a compact matches rail. Opening hierarchy: Strut identity and small studio credit, headline, explanation, CTA, then a prominent product preview showing Mabel's profile and the visitor's bucket-assisted portrait thumbnail. On desktop, give the profile preview slightly more width than the copy; on mobile, place it immediately after the CTA with the chicken, distance and decision controls visible together. Follow with three feature passages, each tied to its relevant screen detail, then testimonials and a joined subscription comparison. Proposed artwork one is a paired photograph of the same small rooster: a commanding crop above a fence and the full view revealing his feed bucket. Its purpose is to expose the profile deception. Proposed artwork two shows eight roosters calling across adjacent sleeping coops while a farmer approaches in slippers with folded coop covers. Its purpose is to show the household cost of competing for attention. Individual chicken portraits supply actual discovery content. Keep names, times, prices, messages and subscription limits in live text. Compared with the recent digest, this concept uses misleading self-presentation, purchased romantic validation and competitive paid visibility. The prices escalate access to attention; testimonials recount a sustained physical lie, voluntary meal delivery and a courtship contest interrupted by the farmer. Avoid the digest's collection growth, historical gatekeeping, room booking, video review and territorial elimination mechanisms.

references.reference: County-fair poultry champion portraits and their prize-ribbon displays
references.cues: Proud side-on chicken portraits, carefully arranged feathers, violet ribbon folds, golden prize centers and formal entry labels.
references.application: Photograph each profile chicken with the seriousness of a prize entrant. Use a warm golden field behind the leading portrait, violet selection accents and broad serif headlines. Ribbon shapes appear only in supporting artwork; profile badges retain plain readable labels.

references.reference: Moulded-pulp egg cartons with stamped packing dates and paper flock labels
references.cues: Oat-colored stock, dark violet stamping, shallow compartment divisions and economical blocks of practical information.
references.application: Use an oat background, dark plum text, fine compartment-like rules and rectangular supporting labels. Translate date-stamp clarity into distance, subscription limits and activity times. Keep texture inside photographs and proposed artwork so interface text remains crisp.

audience_design.landing_application: Combine poultry-show portraiture with egg-carton printing in one restrained system: oat #EFE5CC, yolk gold #F3BE3D, violet #60427B, dark plum #2D2530 and pale cream #FFF9EC. Use Fraunces semibold for headlines and Atkinson Hyperlegible for explanations, prices and controls. Large, carefully lit chicken portraits carry the visual personality. Compose open feature passages around the two explanatory image spreads; use thin rules to connect testimonials and pricing rather than placing every paragraph in a card. The oversized prize-portrait treatment should make the hidden feed bucket feel especially undignified.
audience_design.demo_application: Retain the source service's photo-first discovery stack, bottom decision controls, mutual-match interruption, matches list and private conversation view. Apply the same oat surfaces, violet active states, golden photo backdrops and practical label typography at a denser scale. Keep Pass, Like, Messages, Back and Close plainly labelled. Chicken portraits dominate discovery; chat gives space to readable messages. Use a clear timer and exposure explanation for boosts, with the eight competing roosters shown as activity data. At narrow widths, show one main task at a time while preserving the current profile and conversation state.
